title: Doro wat
steps: Wash the chicken with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt, then leave it for 20 minutes.
Put the onions in a wide heavy pot over medium-low heat with no fat. Cook for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often and adding a splash of water if they stick, until they are reduced, soft and sweet.
Add the niter kibbeh, garlic and ginger and cook for 10 minutes, then stir in the berbere and cook for 15 minutes, until the sauce is a thick dark red paste.
Add the chicken and water, turn to coat, cover and simmer on low for 45 minutes, stirring now and then.
Prick the eggs lightly with a fork and add them. Simmer 10 minutes more, until the sauce is thick and the chicken is tender. Adjust the salt. Serve with injera.
notes: The long cooking of the onions is the secret to the sauce. A tablespoon of tej or white wine can be added with the chicken.

title: Injera
steps: Mix the teff flour with 500 ml of the water in a large bowl. Add the yeast if using. Cover with a cloth and leave at room temperature for 2 to 3 days, until bubbly and sour-smelling. A layer of water forms on top.

Pour off the water on top. Bring 100 ml of the remaining water to a boil, whisk in 3 tbsp of the batter to make a paste, and stir it back into the batter. Add water gradually until it has the consistency of thin crepe batter. Rest 30 minutes and add the salt.
Heat a lightly oiled non-stick pan of about 28 cm over medium heat. Pour in a ladle of batter and swirl in a spiral from the outside in, covering the pan.
Cover and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, without flipping, until the surface is covered in small holes and the edges lift. Slide onto a cloth.
Cool each injera flat, not stacked, before piling them. Cover until serving.
notes: Traditional injera is cooked on a clay mitad; a non-stick pan with a lid is a workable home substitute. Check pure teff flour if gluten matters.

title: Shiro wat
steps: Cook the onion in a dry pan on medium heat for 5 minutes, then add the oil, garlic and berbere and cook another 3 minutes.
Add the tomato if using and cook until soft.
Whisk the shiro powder into the cold water until there are no lumps. Pour into the pan, stirring.
Bring to a simmer, lower the heat and cook for 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick and smooth. Add water if it gets too thick. Season with salt.
Serve hot on injera.
notes: If you cannot find shiro powder, use chickpea flour (besan) with an extra pinch of berbere and a little garlic and ginger powder.

title: Kitfo
steps: Chill the beef well, then chop it by hand or mince it coarsely in a grinder. Keep it cold.
Warm the niter kibbeh gently in a small pan until just melted. Stir in the mitmita and cardamom, off the heat.

Mix the spiced butter into the beef with the salt. Warm very gently in a pan for 1 to 2 minutes if you want it leb leb (warmed), or cook further, until done to your liking, for a fully cooked version.
Serve with cottage cheese, injera and a side of gomen.
notes: If serving raw, use the freshest beef from a trusted butcher. Cook through for children, pregnant guests or if unsure of the meat.

title: Beef tibs
steps: Heat a wide pan very hot and add the niter kibbeh and onions. Cook for 3 minutes until just softened.
Add the beef in a single layer and sear without stirring for 2 minutes, then toss and cook for another 4 minutes.
Add the garlic, chilli, rosemary and berbere and tomato if using. Cook for 3 minutes more until the meat is browned and the liquid has cooked off.
Season and serve immediately with injera.

title: Misir wat
steps: Cook the onions in a dry pot over medium heat for 8 minutes, stirring, adding a splash of water if they stick.
Add the oil, garlic and ginger and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in the berbere and tomato paste and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the lentils and water. Bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 25 minutes, stirring often, until the lentils are completely soft and the stew is thick.
Season with salt and serve with injera.

title: Gomen
steps: Boil the collards in salted water for 10 minutes, then drain well and squeeze out the water.
Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger and chilli and cook for 2 minutes. Add the collards and the water.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, until the greens are very tender and the liquid has gone. Season with salt and serve.
notes: Swap the oil for niter kibbeh on non-fasting days.

title: Tej
steps: Sterilise a large glass jar (4 l) with boiling water and let it cool.
Boil 500 ml of the water with the gesho for 10 minutes, then cool completely.
Dissolve the honey in 500 ml of warm water, add the rest of the water, and add the cooled gesho tea with the gesho. Add the yeast if using.
Cover the jar with a cloth or fit an airlock. Leave in a warm place for 2 to 4 weeks, stirring briefly every few days if using a cloth.
When bubbling slows and the taste is as dry as you like, strain, bottle and refrigerate. Drink within a few weeks.
notes: Strength and sweetness depend on fermentation time. Fermentation produces gas, so keep the jar vented.

title: Buna
steps: Rinse the green beans and dry them. Roast in a heavy pan over medium heat for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring or shaking constantly, until dark brown and shiny with a little oil.
Let the beans cool for a few minutes, then grind finely with a mortar and pestle or a grinder.
Heat the water in a jebena or small pot until boiling. Add the ground coffee and stir.
Bring back to a boil, remove from the heat for a minute, and repeat twice more. Let it settle for 2 minutes without stirring.
Pour slowly into small cups and add sugar if you like. Serve with popcorn or bread, and refill twice.
notes: In the full ceremony, incense is burned and the coffee is served in three rounds.

title: Firfir

ingredients.note: stale or fresh, torn into 3 cm pieces

steps: Cook the onion in a dry pan over medium heat for 5 minutes, then add the oil and garlic and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the berbere and tomato and cook for 3 minutes. Add the water and simmer for 5 minutes to make a loose sauce.
Add the injera pieces and toss for 2 to 3 minutes until they have soaked up the sauce.
Season with salt and serve right away, with a spoon or more injera.
notes: Non-fasting versions use niter kibbeh instead of oil or add chopped cooked meat.
